our_answer: m(m-1)...(m-n+1) a^n (ax+b)^{m-n}; = m!/(m-n)! a^n (ax+b)^{m-n} when m is a positive integer with m >= n
book_answer: d^n y/dx^n = m! a^n (ax+b)^{m-n}/(m-n)! if m>0, m>n;  = 0 if m>0, m<n;  = n! a^n if m>0, m=n
evidence: Same mathematics; ours states the single general falling-factorial form, the book splits it into three cases. Verified our form against sympy's actual k-th derivative for k=1..4 with symbolic m (exact match). The book's cases are then consequences of it: (a) m>n -- ff(m,n) - m!/(m-n)! simplifies to exactly 0; (b) m a positive integer < n -- sympy's k-th derivative is 0 and our falling factorial contains a zero factor, so both give 0 (checked m=3,4 for k=m+1..m+3); (c) m=n -- sympy's n-th derivative equals n! a^n equals our form (checked m=2,3,5). No disagreement.
